title: Universal Program Emits the Tableau Circuit
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state multitape Turing machine with Boolean input and output, let $n,T\in\mathbb N$, and let $z$ be a finite bit string, with $T\ge 1$. The counter program constructed from $M$, started at its initial label with all 11 registers zero and read position zero, on the input consisting of $n$ ones, then a zero, then $T$ ones, then a zero, followed by $z$, reaches a halted state with some register assignment and input position, and has printed the encoding of the tableau circuit for $M$, $n$, $z$, and $T$; this is achieved within the stated run bound.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state multitape Turing machine over Boolean symbols
caveat: The theorem uses repository-defined constructions for the counter program, tableau circuit, encoding, and run bound; their full meanings are not supplied by the informal descriptions.
